Places don’t make great artists. Artists make great places.

This fellowship develops nationally relevant infrastructure that increases hyperlocal power. It will turn Carly Heath’s established practice across nightlife culture, creative production, public policy and delivery into a field-backed argument, a tested first method, an investable Nightlife Culture institution and a fundable next phase.

Why all six work packages are necessary:
WP1 governs the inquiry; it prevents the programme from becoming an accumulation of attractive but untestable ideas.
WP2 supplies lived and place evidence; it tests the people/place thesis beyond Carly’s prior experience.
WP3 follows value and power; it adds economic, ownership and investment questions that WP2 alone cannot answer.
WP4 converts insight into a testable user-facing evidence layer; it is the method R&D phase, not a second research phase.
WP5 develops the institution capable of carrying the method; it separates organisational design from tool design.
WP6 synthesises, mobilises and defines the next funded phase; it ensures learning reaches decisions and does not remain an internal research archive.
